target: workflow.sh diff/merge — the same region name with owner=plugin in the project but owner=project in the template is a conflict, not a merge
cmd: source "$PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/lib/workflow.sh"; source "$FIXTURES/workflow-fixture.sh"; wf_file project.js '// top' '// @agentic-loop:begin region=shared owner=plugin' 'console.log("plugin owned in project");' '// @agentic-loop:end region=shared' '// bottom'; wf_file template.js '// top' '// @agentic-loop:begin region=shared owner=project' 'console.log("now project owned upstream");' '// @agentic-loop:end region=shared' '// bottom'; cp project.js expected.js; DIFF=$(workflow_diff project.js template.js '//' '{}'); MERGE=$(workflow_merge project.js template.js '//' '{}'); MATCH=$(cmp -s project.js expected.js && echo true || echo false); jq -n --argjson d "$DIFF" --argjson m "$MERGE" --argjson match "$MATCH" '{diff:$d, merge:$m, match:$match}'
_note: region= is the only identity the merge trusts, but ownership itself can disagree between project and template (e.g. upstream reclassified a region from plugin- to project-owned). That disagreement must surface as a conflict rather than silently replacing project content or silently keeping it as if nothing changed — checked against the actual reason string the code emits.
